answer.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and prior archived experience (memory_31, memory_86) shows signup/onboarding simplification produces durable activation lift for the self-serve/SMB segment most exposed to the competitor's pricing move. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 lets me confirm whether onboarding or in-product activation messaging had the stronger, more durable effect before committing the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing is explicitly flagged as risky: memory_73 shows a similar discount drove short-term signups and revenue but eroded retention by 12%, making it unsustainable and a poor fit for the objective of long-term qualified revenue, even though competitive pressure makes it tempting. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are valuable but don't address the acute, quantified drops in activation/onboarding this week. Running this as a standard (not broad) experiment preserves the ability to see real effect size before wider rollout, especially since inherited memories are being treated as directional evidence rather than certainty.
